source_anchors: The “top-down” strategy yielded microbial community Y13.
The 13th transfer was used as the top-down inoculum in this study.
The bottom-up synthetic consortium (M) was rationally constructed following function-based SynCom (synthetic community) design strategies ( 17 , 21 ).

The consortium comprised the obligate organohalide-respiring bacterium Dehalococcoides mccartyi , supported by the corrinoid-provisioning strains Geobacter lovleyi and Sulfurospirillum multivorans ( 9 , 18 ), the fermentative supplier Petrimonas sulfuriphila PET ( 22 ), and seven isolated γ-HCH-degrading strains, several of which harbor cobalamin synthesis genes ( 23 ).

Specifically, Enterococcus avium ATCC 14025 shared an ANI of 98.03 with PseS3 and 98.21 with bin161. Enterococcus thailandicus DSM 21767 exhibited an ANI of 99.35 with R1, 99.31 with R3, and 99.35 with bin381. Similarly, Enterococcus casseliflavus ATCC 49996 shared an ANI of 98.24 with R12 and 98.24 with bin436.

Additionally, it should be noted that the initial consortium was constructed by directly mixing glycerol stocks of individual strains without prior revival and verification of each strain’s viability. The OD 600 data reported here reflect the overall growth of the enrichment culture and do not confirm that all component strains were equally revived.

To further investigate the genomic characteristics of Enterococcus spp., the Enterococcus MAGs (bin161, bin381, and bin436) assembled in this study were compared with whole genomes of Enterococcus spp., including PseS3, R1, R3, R12, and standard strains such as Enterococcus avium ATCC 14025, Enterococcus thailandicus DSM 21767, and Enterococcus casseliflavus ATCC 49996, which were obtained from NCBI.

changes.before: Functional anaerobic organochlorine-degrading bacterial consortia (top-down consortium M and bottom-up consortium Y13) constructed around generalist non-obligate organochlorine-degrading Enterococcus strains (Enterococcus casseliflavus PseS3, R1, R3, R12) alongside organohalide-respiring and fermentative partners (Sulfurospirillum multivorans, Trichlorobacter lovleyi, Dehalococcoides mccartyi, and Petrimonas sulfuriphila) for gamma-hexachlorocyclohexane (lindane) bioremediation in coastal wetland sediment microcosms while suppressing CO2-reduction methanogenesis.
changes.after: Two anaerobic lindane bioaugmentation treatments in coastal wetland sediment: top-down sediment enrichment Y13 and bottom-up consortium M. M was assembled from Dehalococcoides mccartyi, Geobacter lovleyi (represented here as Trichlorobacter lovleyi), Sulfurospirillum multivorans, Petrimonas sulfuriphila PET and seven isolated gamma-HCH degraders. The five retained taxonomy entries are a partial representation, not a complete shared roster of M and Y13. The Enterococcus casseliflavus entry corresponds to isolate R12; PseS3 is E. avium and R1/R3 are E. thailandicus. Intended inoculum membership does not establish revival or endpoint colonization of every stock. The ecological interaction graph retains separate unresolved mechanism limitations.

changes.before: Generalist non-obligate organochlorine-degrading Enterococcus (strains PseS3, R1, R3, R12) that colonizes sediment microcosms and degrades gamma-HCH.
changes.after: The source ANI comparison identifies isolate R12 as Enterococcus casseliflavus (98.24% ANI to ATCC 49996). Sediment MAG bin436 has the same reported ANI to that reference but is a separate metagenomic reconstruction, not the R12 isolate. PseS3 is E. avium and R1/R3 are E. thailandicus; these other isolates must not be grouped under this E. casseliflavus descriptor. The current five-entry taxonomy is incomplete for consortium M and does not define a complete Y13 roster.

changes.before: Identifies Enterococcus casseliflavus (strain R12 / bin436, 98.24% ANI to ATCC 49996) alongside E. avium and E. thailandicus as the isolated non-obligate organochlorine-degrading Enterococcus strains in the consortium.
changes.after: The ANI comparison separately identifies isolate R12 and sediment MAG bin436 as E. casseliflavus relative to ATCC 49996 (98.24% each). It assigns PseS3 to E. avium and R1/R3 to E. thailandicus. Species correspondence does not establish that R12 and bin436 are the same physical strain or genome.

changes.before: Obligate organohalide-respiring bacterium included in the bottom-up γ-HCH-degrading consortium Y13.
changes.after: Obligate organohalide-respiring bacterium included in the bottom-up gamma-HCH-degrading consortium M. Intended inoculum membership does not establish strain-specific revival or endpoint sediment colonization.

discussion.prompt: Complete the separate M and Y13 membership descriptions without equating inoculated stocks with sediment MAGs or endpoint establishment.
discussion.rationale: Methods identify Y13 as the thirteenth sediment-enrichment transfer and M as a bottom-up mixture of four named partner taxa plus seven isolated degraders. The five current entries therefore represent selected taxa rather than a complete common roster. R12 and bin436 share a species-level ANI assignment but remain an isolate and a sediment MAG, respectively. Bulk revival measurements cannot establish viability of every initial stock.
